subject.title: [Feature]: optional 1Password plugin — approval-gated, audited agent secrets broker

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor and bundle this 1Password secrets broker, or require it to prove itself first as an externally maintained ClawHub plugin?
rationale: Current policy normally routes optional commercial-service integrations outside core, while this proposal argues for a security-sensitive bundled exception requiring durable ownership, threat modeling, dependency selection, and release support.

options.title: External proof first
options.body: Develop and publish a ClawHub code plugin, gather live security and workflow proof, and revisit official or bundled promotion only after the ownership case is established.

options.title: Sponsor a bundled plugin
options.body: Accept the integration as a maintained security surface and require named ownership, threat modeling, upgrade policy, dependency review, and comprehensive live proof before implementation lands.

options.title: Narrow the proposal
options.body: Keep only a vendor-neutral audited secret-broker contract in scope if implementation discovers a concrete missing plugin API that cannot be provided externally.

recommendation.title: External proof first
recommendation.body: Develop and publish a ClawHub code plugin, gather live security and workflow proof, and revisit official or bundled promotion only after the ownership case is established.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available owner signal combines authorship of this proposal with authorship of the repository's current plugin and bundling scope policy.
